findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Coverage by any 2 shared stems lets the criteria of sibling parts cover a part that was silently omitted. The goal's 'silent split' is then accepted, and no fixture tests it.
findings.evidence: Take the existing request numbered-dot-parts (refusal_corpus.rs:1710-1715). Part 3, 'Cover the flag with a test', has the stems {cover, flag}, since 'test' is a stop word. That is n=2, so 1 shared stem is required. The criterion for part 1, 'Add a --json flag to athena status', shares 'flag', so part 3 counts as covered. A reading with criteria for parts 1 and 2 only, and no deferral sentence, is accepted. The sza7 parts all concern timed-out checks, so a criterion for part 2 shares 2 stems with part 3 the same way. Every refusing demonstration either adds a deferral phrase (criteria 1, 3 and 5) or uses the unrelated stock criterion (numbered-paren-parts-uncovered). None shows a silently omitted part whose wording overlaps its siblings. Fix: Measure each item against the stems that belong to it alone: drop stems that also appear in other items of the same request, or weight stems by how rare they are across the items. Require the overlap on those stems (fall back to all stems only when an item has none of its own). Add Refuse cases where a reading silently omits part 3: numbered-dot-parts with criteria for parts 1 and 2 only, and the sza7 request with no deferral sentence. Keep the long-title Steward Accept case as the counter-check.
findings.location: Approach / Decision 2 (coverage = min(2, ceil(n/2)) shared stems with any criterion); Demonstrations 1-3

findings.summary: The '<adjective> <noun>' permission shape fires on ordinary modal sentences that are not about splitting, and such a sentence exempts every item. This is the same class of false exemption as the earlier major finding 2.
findings.evidence: Shape (1) needs only a modal, no negation, no complaint word, and an adjective from {separate, follow-up, later, next, smaller, several, multiple} followed by a noun from {job, change, PR, request, part}. Sentences such as 'A wrong count could block the next job.', 'This bug can stall multiple jobs.' and 'The fix might need a smaller change.' match. They name no marker, and 'one that names none exempts every item', so the whole gate is switched off for that request. The planned negative table only has split/separately sentences and complaints. Fix: Require a verb that moves work (split, move, defer, leave, do, handle, ship, land) whose destination is the adjective-noun phrase ('in/into/as/to a separate job'), or a part as the subject of 'be/become a follow-up job'. Add 'A wrong count could block the next job.' and 'This can stall multiple jobs.' to the negative table and as corpus Refuse cases.
findings.location: Approach, split exemption shape (1); Decision 3; Step 3; Demonstration 5

findings.summary: Deferral phrases in the summary and assumptions refuse retry readings that only recount the earlier split. Those retries are the main population this gate serves.
findings.evidence: An item is refused when it is 'deferred or uncovered'. A deferral is a sentence with a phrase such as follow-up or deferred plus a marker, and the only negation guard words are never, without, refus, unless and do not. A typical retry reading says 'The earlier job deferred part (3) to a follow-up job; this reading covers it.' That sentence has a phrase, the marker (3) and no guard word, so the reading is refused even though its criteria cover part (3). The complaint guard (earlier, previous, said, wrong) is applied only to request sentences. No Accept fixture has a reading that mentions a past deferral. Fix: Apply the complaint/past guard to reading sentences too: earlier, previous, was, had, a job id, 'the last reading'. Alternatively, count a summary or assumptions deferral only for items that are also uncovered, and keep the rule that an out_of_scope item naming a marker counts without a phrase. Add an Accept corpus case: a retry reading whose summary recounts the earlier deferral of (3) and whose criteria cover (3).
findings.location: Approach, deferral rule; Decision 4; Risks (third bullet)

findings.summary: The plan does not say whether the stop list is checked before or after the cut to 5 characters, and the two orders give different results.
findings.evidence: The stop list holds full words ('described', 'existing', 'change'), but stems are cut to 5 characters ('descr', 'exist', 'chang'). If the stop check runs on the cut stem, these entries never match. The Steward bullet 'The change is made as described: <title>' then gains the generic stems chang and descr, and any criterion containing 'change ... made' covers it. The refusing_check doc (checks.rs:509) already lists 'stop-list and stem order' as a past gap. Fix: State that the stop check runs on the raw lowercased token before the plural drop and the cut, or store the stop list in stem form. Pin 'changes', 'described' and 'existing' as not distinctive in the stem unit test.

findings.summary: It is unclear whether the 'Acceptance:' label line counts as the 'Acceptance heading' that limits which bullets are read.
findings.evidence: StewardRequest::new writes the plain label line 'Acceptance:' followed by '- ' bullets and 'Files:' (steward.rs:581-585), not a '#' heading. Step 2 drops '#' heading lines and says the section 'ends at the next heading or label line'. It does not say that the 'Acceptance:' label opens the section. Fix: Say that a line equal to 'Acceptance:' (in any case), or a '#' heading whose text is Acceptance, opens the section. Add a request_parts unit test on a from_change render whose body holds a non-acceptance dash line.

findings.summary: The stated basis, a count of corpus Accept cases with parts, does not measure the newly refused share of past readings, which is the figure the replay hold applies.
findings.evidence: replay_limit_percent(Some(5)) = 10 (replay.rs:304-307). At verification the replay checks the newest 50 accepted readings. Corpus Accept cases are built so the gate accepts them, so counting them says nothing about how many real readings the gate will now refuse. The heuristic may refuse more than 10% of real readings, given Steward bullets and retries. Fix: Take the basis from the replay that runs inside the producer's loop (it reports the newly refused share against the same limit), or label the 5% plainly as an unmeasured estimate. Note in the doc comment that the hold limit is the declared share plus 5 points.

findings.summary: The fake reader copies request lines verbatim, markers included, so the copied criteria can trip earlier checks, and the fix is not tested against them.
findings.evidence: The copied criteria keep their '- ', '1. ' or '(1) ' prefix. The fake producer and verifier parse criteria by splitting on '. ' (fake.rs:328-338, 391-394). A request bullet such as 'touch no other file', copied as a criterion, can be refused by check_scope_limit (PROPOSAL_REQUEST at reading.rs:8445 has that shape), so the reading is refused earlier than before. Fix: Strip the marker before copying. Have the new fake.rs unit test run check_reading_text, or the fake's reading through the gate, on a bullet request to show the fake's reading is accepted end to end.

findings.summary: A negation anywhere in a sentence blocks a real permission that sits in another clause of it.
findings.evidence: In '(1) and (2) cannot wait; (3) may be a follow-up job.' the word 'cannot' rules out the whole sentence. Fix: Apply the negation and complaint guards per clause (split on ';' and ','), as the deferral rule already does.

summary: The plan fits the request and the reading. It adds one last step! line to refusing_check (checks.rs:546 exists), adds a separate request_parts parser so is_bullet and request_text_acceptance stay untouched, builds the Steward fixture with the real StewardRequest::from_change (steward.rs:620-624), and fixes the fixed-reading seams it found (fake.rs:311 and common/mod.rs:572). Its demonstrations name real seams and would fail without the behaviour. The dependents list matches the callers I grepped: reading.rs:722, replay.rs:55, steward.rs:424, main.rs:687, drain.rs:4431/4451, and the step-order tests at reading.rs:4907, 5389, 7412, 8111 and 8489, all of which survive a last-position step. The matching rules have three soundness problems. (1) An item counts as covered when any criterion shares at most 2 stems with it. Parts of one request share topic words, so a part that is silently left out is covered by the criteria of the parts next to it. That is the very 'silently split' case the goal names, and no fixture tests it. (2) The split-permission shape '<adjective> <noun> plus a modal' also matches ordinary sentences such as 'could block the next job', which would exempt every item. (3) Deferral phrases in the summary and assumptions refuse retry readings that only recount an earlier deferral. Smaller problems: the order of stop-list check and stem cut is not specified, it is unclear whether the 'Acceptance:' label counts as a heading, and the stated basis for the 5% figure is not a measure of past readings.
